en.title: Same Heatpump. Why you pay more?
en.standfirst: One product, five countries — an expense gap that engineering cannot explain.
lead: A four-person household in an existing house needs roughly 8 kW of heating with hot water. That requirement does not change at a border. This report asks what does.

We chose one product — Daikin Altherma 3 R F, 8 kW with a 230-litre cylinder, Europe's highest-volume air/water heat pump, neither a budget import nor a premium line — and followed it through five markets. Our own catalogue shows it registered in all five with the same specification: 8.3 kW rated, SCOP 4.95, R32, 56 dB(A). From there, every euro comes from a named source.
The household's bill runs from €11,829 in Britain to €34,053 in Germany — 2.9 times. Of the €22,224 between them, the heat pump accounts for €37. Installation accounts for €16,750; VAT for €5,437.

bullets.label: United Kingdom
bullets.text: Heat pump €7,579 · installation €4,250 · VAT 0% · the household pays €11,829.

en.title: Europe's Heating Transition: Five Markets, Five Realities
en.standfirst: HeatPump DataBase Europe launches its new monthly Special Report series, combining verified market data, policy developments and the latest 2026 heat-pump signals across Europe's major heating markets.
lead: Europe's heating transition is accelerating, but the pace, technology mix and policy environment remain markedly different from one country to another.

The inaugural HeatPump DataBase Europe Special Report — “Europe's Heating Transition: Five Markets, Five Realities” — examines the latest available market evidence from Germany, the United Kingdom, France, Poland and Italy, combining 2025 full-year market data with the newest available 2026 indicators through August.

At the European level, heat-pump sales returned to growth in 2025, with approximately 2.9 million units sold across 21 European countries and an installed stock of around 29.3 million units. The national picture, however, remains far more complex.

bullets.label: Germany
bullets.text: Heat pumps became the country's largest individual heating-technology category in 2025, while H1 2026 sales reached 194,500 units, up 40% year on year.

bullets.label: United Kingdom
bullets.text: Hydronic heat-pump sales continued to rise, but boilers still dominate the heating market and the gap between product sales and actual retrofit deployment remains significant.

bullets.label: France
bullets.text: The hydronic heating market has contracted substantially since 2021, while the apparent heat-pump share increasingly reflects a shrinking overall market rather than rapid growth in absolute heat-pump volume.

bullets.label: Poland
bullets.text: The market is showing renewed momentum in 2026, with H1 heating heat-pump sell-in up 18%, although inventory effects and differences in market definitions remain essential to understanding the data.

bullets.label: Italy
bullets.text: Boiler demand declined sharply in 2025, while the latest H1 2026 data show air-to-water heat-pump volumes up 25.5%, signalling stronger momentum in electrified heating solutions.
